spots.title: Three dora and an 8-tile wait, kept dama
spots.situation: East 2, turn 8. You are the dealer, fourth at 22,700. You draw [[4p]] into tenpai: cut [[7s]] and you wait on [[5m]]-[[8m]] with 8 tiles live. The hand is tanyao with three [[2m]] as dora. Nobody has declared. Kamicha has ponned [[C]] and [[F]].
spots.did: You cut [[7s]] and stayed dama. The hand won by tsumo for 12,000.
spots.luckyj: LuckyJ declares 95% of first closed tenpais with 8 or more live tiles before turn 10. Two dragon pons across the table do not stop it: in the 22 hands where an opponent already showed two dragon pons, it still declared 16 times, including all 3 with 8 or more live tiles. That sample is small.
spots.fix: Declare. Dama caps this hand at a dealer mangan, 12,000, on ron or tsumo. Riichi makes the same tsumo a haneman, 18,000, and gives a ron the same chance through ura dora and ippatsu. The cost is having to cut a drawn haku [[P]] into the two dragon pons. LuckyJ wins about 60% of its riichi hands with 8 or more live tiles.

spots.title: Pinfu on an 8-tile wait at turn 6, kept dama
spots.situation: South 2, two honba, turn 6. You are third at 19,100. You draw [[1s]] and reach tenpai: cut [[7p]] and you wait on [[5s]]-[[8s]], 8 tiles live. The hand is pinfu and nothing else. The dealer has ponned [[S]]; nobody has declared.
spots.did: You stayed dama. The hand won by tsumo for 2,100.
spots.luckyj: LuckyJ declares 95% of first closed tenpais with 8 or more live tiles before turn 10.
spots.fix: Riichi. Before the honba, dama pays 1,000 on a ron and 1,500 on a tsumo. Riichi pays 2,000 and 2,700, before ura dora. A one-han hand on a two-sided wait at turn 6 is the hand riichi exists for.

spots.title: The better tile was also the safer one
spots.situation: South 1, turn 6. Kamicha, leading with 46,000, has ponned haku [[P]]. You are third at 21,500, 3-shanten with two dora, and draw [[2m]].
spots.did: You cut the [[2m]] you drew. It left 36 tiles of acceptance and was live against the pon. It dealt in for 1,000.
spots.fix: [[S]] leaves 38 tiles and has two other copies showing, so only a tanki can hit it. When the safer tile is also the more efficient one, it is the only cut.

spots.title: Turn 13, a free honor in hand
spots.situation: South 1, turn 13 with 18 tiles left. Kamicha, leading with 36,700, has ponned [[3p]]. You are third at 18,300 and 1-shanten after a closed kan of [[1p]].
spots.did: You cut the [[7m]] you drew, live against the pon, and dealt in for 3,900.
spots.luckyj: When a safe tile keeps the same shanten and acceptance against a single call, LuckyJ takes it 83% of the time at 1-shanten from turn 13 on.
spots.fix: [[C]] leaves the same 12 tiles and has two other copies showing. Take it.

spots.title: All last, tied for first
spots.situation: South 4, turn 9. You and toimen are tied for first at 33,600. The dealer, third at 23,500, has ponned haku [[P]]. You are 1-shanten with a chi and two red fives.
spots.did: You cut the [[9m]] you drew, live against the dealer, and paid 1,500. The dealer's win also kept the game going.
spots.luckyj: Against a single call LuckyJ takes a free safe tile 69% of the time at 1-shanten on turns 9 to 12.
spots.fix: [[N]] leaves the same 6 tiles and has two other copies showing. In all last with first place on the line, a free safe tile is never optional.

spots.title: 8,000 from a tile that was not even the most efficient
spots.situation: East 1, turn 7. Toimen ponned [[N]], their seat wind, then added the fourth [[N]] as a kan, and has kept cutting tiles from hand since. You are 2-shanten with a pair of [[F]] and two dora.
spots.did: You cut [[4m]], only half suji against the kan because just the [[7m]] side was covered, leaving 20 tiles of acceptance, and dealt in for 8,000.
spots.luckyj: Against a single call, LuckyJ pays one or two tiles of acceptance for a safe tile about a quarter of the time. Here the safe tile cost nothing against the tile you chose.
spots.fix: [[F]] leaves 21 tiles, one more than [[4m]]. With your other [[F]] and the one in kamicha's river, only a tanki on the last copy can hit it. [[8m]] and [[2p]] leave 22 but are live too. A kan of a value wind is a hand with its yaku done: take the honor.

spots.title: Four more tiles, and genbutsu
spots.situation: South 3, one honba, turn 11. The dealer has ponned [[3m]]. You are fourth at 19,300, 2-shanten, with a [[2s]] pon and the dora, haku [[P]].
spots.did: You cut [[3p]], live, leaving 10 tiles. On the next turn no safe tile kept the hand, and [[2p]] dealt in for 1,800.
spots.fix: [[4s]] is genbutsu and leaves 14 tiles, because three [[2s]] sit in your own pon and the fourth is in the dealer's river, so [[3s]][[4s]] can only take [[5s]]. [[E]] is genbutsu with 14 as well. Count a shape's live tiles before you protect it.

spots.title: Two pons across the table and a live honor
spots.situation: South 1, turn 8. You are the dealer, second at 21,500, and you have just ponned haku [[P]]. Toimen has ponned [[S]], the round wind, and [[5m]] with the red five.
spots.did: After the pon you cut [[C]], an honor with no other copy showing, and dealt in for 2,000. Toimen was waiting on it alone.
spots.luckyj: Against two calls LuckyJ cuts a live tile only about 30% of the time from turn 9 on when a safe tile keeps its shanten.
spots.fix: [[8p]] is genbutsu and leaves 41 tiles against 43. A hand built from pons often ends on a tanki or a shanpon, so a live honor is one of the likeliest tiles to hit it. Pay the two tiles.

spots.title: Twelve discards and not one sou
spots.situation: South 2, turn 12. You lead with 43,300. Shimocha, last at 6,300, has ponned [[F]] and chied [[2s]][[3s]][[4s]], and has discarded twelve tiles without a single sou. You are open tenpai on a [[6m]] kanchan and draw [[9s]].
spots.did: You cut the [[9s]] and dealt in for 7,700 to a sou honitsu.
spots.fix: A dragon pon, a sou chi and a river with no sou is a honitsu, and its waits are sou. Fold with the red [[5mr]], genbutsu. It costs the tenpai and a red five from a 3-han hand. With an 11,000-point lead, the deal-in costs more.

frames.note: Kamicha has just discarded [[2p]], so [[2p]] is now genbutsu against both players. [[3s]] is safe against the riichi, because toimen passed it after the declaration, and live against kamicha's pon.
[[1s]] is genbutsu against kamicha and only suji against the riichi. [[2p]] is still genbutsu against both.

spots.title: The tile that was safe against both players
spots.situation: East 4, one honba. You lead with 40,800. Shimocha declared riichi on turn 4 and kamicha has ponned haku [[P]]. You are folding at 2-shanten.
spots.did: You cut [[3s]] on turn 12 and [[1s]] on turn 13. The [[1s]] completed shimocha's shanpon for 1,600.
spots.luckyj: At 2-shanten against a riichi, LuckyJ keeps a safe tile 96% of the time when one holds its shanten. You already fold that often. The leak here is which safe tile.
spots.fix: Rank the safe tiles before you cut: genbutsu against every threat, then genbutsu against the riichi, then an honor with two other copies showing, then suji, with a 1 or 9 on suji the safest of those. Suji only rules out a two-sided wait; shanpon, tanki and kanchan still hit it. [[2p]] topped that list for two turns and cost two or three tiles of acceptance in a hand that was folding anyway.

spots.title: The safe tile that also kept the better hand
spots.situation: East 1, turn 10. Shimocha declared riichi on the turn before. You are second at 25,000, 2-shanten with two dora ([[F]] and the red [[5pr]]) and a pair of [[N]].
spots.did: You broke the [[N]] pair. No other [[N]] is showing, so a shanpon or tanki on it is still possible, and it left 20 tiles of acceptance.
spots.fix: [[2m]] is genbutsu and leaves 43 tiles. When a safe tile is also the better tile for the hand, there is nothing to weigh.

spots.title: 2-shanten on turn 13 against a riichi
spots.situation: East 2, one honba, turn 13 with 23 tiles left. You are the dealer and lead with 34,700. Toimen declared riichi on turn 6 and kamicha has ponned [[F]]. You are 2-shanten.
spots.did: You cut [[8p]], live against both players, to keep 2-shanten.
spots.luckyj: At 2-shanten on turn 13 or later, LuckyJ cuts a live tile against a riichi 5.0% of the time.
spots.fix: Fold with [[7s]], suji against both players, or [[3p]], genbutsu against both. Either costs a shanten. From 2-shanten with about five draws left the hand rarely reaches tenpai at all, so that shanten was worth little, and a leading dealer has more to lose from a deal-in than from a folded hand.

spots.title: Genbutsu against the riichi that also kept more tiles
spots.situation: South 1, one honba, turn 16 with 6 tiles left. Kamicha declared riichi on turn 11, shimocha has two calls and toimen one. You are third at 20,100 and 2-shanten.
spots.did: You cut [[5s]]: nakasuji against the riichi, and only half suji against the two open hands, which both hold sou melds.
spots.luckyj: Against one riichi, LuckyJ's nakasuji cuts dealt into it 2.8 times per 100 and its genbutsu never did.
spots.fix: [[3p]] is genbutsu against the riichi and leaves more acceptance, 32 tiles against 26. Neither tile is safe against the open hands. [[7p]] is suji against all three players, but it is a 3-7 suji, the weakest kind, against the riichi.

spots.title: Two riichis: check the tile against both
spots.situation: South 2, one honba, turn 16 with 7 tiles left. Shimocha and kamicha are both in riichi. You are second at 23,400 and 1-shanten.
spots.did: You cut [[8m]]: genbutsu against kamicha, live against shimocha.
spots.luckyj: When a safe tile leaves exactly the same shanten and acceptance, LuckyJ pushes past it about 2% of the time at 1-shanten.
spots.fix: [[6m]] is genbutsu against both riichis and leaves the same 10 tiles. With two riichis, check every tile against each river separately.

spots.title: An 8-tile open tenpai, folded
spots.situation: South 3, turn 10. Kamicha declared riichi on turn 4. You are third at 24,500, open with two chis and a concealed [[F]] triplet, and you draw the red [[5sr]].
spots.did: You cut [[6m]], genbutsu, and gave up the tenpai.
spots.luckyj: With an open tenpai against a riichi, where keeping it needs a dangerous tile, LuckyJ pushes 93% of the time with 8 or more live tiles, and 91% of the time when such a hand is only 1 or 2 han.
spots.fix: Cut the red [[5sr]] and wait on [[5m]]-[[8m]] with 8 tiles. It costs a han and leaves [[F]] and the red [[5pr]], about 2,000 points. An 8-tile wait with a yaku is the tenpai you push.

spots.title: A tenpai that could not win by ron
spots.situation: South 2, turn 14 with 14 tiles left. Kamicha has just declared riichi and shimocha has ponned [[4s]]. You are fourth at 20,800 and draw [[3p]] into tenpai.
spots.did: You cut [[2s]], live against the riichi, to wait on [[4s]]. The hand has no yaku, so it could only win by tsumo, and three [[4s]] were already in shimocha's pon: one tile in the whole game could complete it. The [[2s]] dealt in for 8,000.
spots.luckyj: LuckyJ pushes 43% of its tenpai hands against a riichi, you 38%. What decides the push is the yaku: LuckyJ pushes 86% of its open tenpais that have a yaku on the wait, and 55% of those with none.
spots.fix: Fold with [[2p]], genbutsu against the riichi and suji against shimocha. Cutting the red [[5sr]] for a [[1s]]-[[4s]] wait does not help: all four [[1s]] are gone. A yakuless dama with one live tile is worth about as much as a 1-shanten hand.

spots.title: The free cut that kept a mangan in reach
spots.situation: South 3, turn 5. You lead with 29,500. On turn 4 you ponned [[S]], the round wind and your seat wind, for 2 han. Your one dora is the red [[5sr]], and eleven of your fourteen tiles are souzu or honors. You draw [[5m]].
spots.did: You cut [[2s]] and kept [[4m]]-[[5m]] and the lone [[4p]]. More souzu followed it out over the next turns, and the hand was still 1-shanten at the draw.
spots.luckyj: When a first call leaves eleven or more of the fourteen tiles in one suit plus honors, and every dora in hand fits that suit, LuckyJ finishes the flush 59% of the time and wins one hand in five with it, for about 10,000.
spots.fix: Cut [[4p]]. It leaves the same 2-shanten and the same 15 tiles of acceptance as [[2s]], and it keeps the flush open. Double South, honitsu and the red five are 5 han, a mangan. Without the flush the hand is 3 han.

frames.note: Shimocha shows all three tells: two calls, the second one late, and five draws in a row thrown straight from the wall since. [[S]] is the tile you just drew.
Shimocha has thrown a sixth straight draw from the wall. [[S]] is still the safest tile and keeps the most acceptance.

spots.title: Two live cuts into a caller showing all three tells
spots.situation: East 1, turn 16, all four players on 25,000. Your two [[1p]] are dora, and you ponned [[9s]] on turn 5. Shimocha ponned [[C]], then chied your red [[5sr]] on turn 10, and has thrown every draw since straight from the wall. You are 1-shanten and draw [[S]].
spots.did: You cut [[7m]], then [[6m]] on turn 17, both live against shimocha. You reached tenpai with a [[F]] pon on turn 18 and dealt in to shimocha with [[4m]] on turn 19 for 3,900.
spots.luckyj: With all three tells showing, the caller is tenpai 84% of the time in LuckyJ's games. At 1-shanten with a safe tile in hand, LuckyJ then cuts a live tile 32% of the time.
spots.fix: Cut [[S]] both turns. On turn 16 it keeps 1-shanten with 10 tiles of acceptance, twice what [[7m]] keeps, and with two other copies showing only a tanki can hit it. The hand still improves on [[5m]], [[8m]], [[1p]] and [[F]] without handing shimocha a live tile.

spots.title: A free genbutsu against a caller showing all three tells
spots.situation: East 4, one honba, turn 14. You are the dealer, second on 23,100, 1-shanten with the [[8p]] dora and a [[3s]]-[[4s]]-[[5s]] chi. Shimocha ponned [[1m]], chied your [[7m]] on turn 8 for a second call, and has thrown five straight draws from the wall since. Kamicha has one chi. You draw [[3p]].
spots.did: You cut the [[3p]] you drew, live against both callers. Nobody won, and the hand ended in a draw.
spots.luckyj: At 1-shanten with dora in hand and all three tells showing, LuckyJ cuts a live tile 32% of the time when it holds a safe one. When the safe tile keeps the same shanten and acceptance, it is the only cut.
spots.fix: Cut [[8s]]. It is genbutsu against both callers and leaves the same 1-shanten and 20 tiles of acceptance as [[3p]].

spots.title: Third in the last hand, a live chun into the dealer's flush
spots.situation: South 4, the last hand, turn 9. You are third on 19,800: 5,500 behind second and 7,800 ahead of the dealer, kamicha, in fourth. The dealer has ponned [[1p]] and chied [[6p]]-[[7p]]-[[8p]], a pinzu half flush in the making, and toimen has two calls. You draw [[6s]] into tenpai on [[1m]]-[[4m]] with riichi, pinfu and the [[2m]] dora, but the tile you must cut is a live [[C]].
spots.did: You declared riichi with [[C]]. The dealer was waiting on it and won 5,800 with the half flush and chun, plus your riichi stick. That left the dealer on 18,800 and you on 13,000, in fourth, and you finished the game there.
spots.luckyj: Going into a game's final hand in third, LuckyJ drops to fourth through its own deal-in 3.2% of the time, over 251 such hands.
spots.fix: Cut [[2s]], genbutsu against both callers, and stay at 1-shanten with the chun kept. A win here moves you from third to second, worth about 75 rank points at your level. This deal-in moved you to fourth, which costs about 265 more than third. A live dragon into a two-call half flush that has to win is too big a risk for that trade.

spots.title: An 18,000 fold that was the right fold
spots.situation: East 2, turn 8. You lead with 33,000 and are 2-shanten with an open [[3p]]-[[4p]]-[[5p]] chi. The dealer, toimen, has just declared riichi, and kamicha has chied twice in souzu.
spots.did: You cut [[F]]. Two other copies were showing, so only a single-tile wait could hit it, and it was genbutsu against kamicha. The dealer's seven pairs was waiting on exactly that tile: 18,000 with the half flush, riichi and ippatsu.
spots.luckyj: Against one riichi, LuckyJ's cuts of an honor with two other copies showing deal in 0.2 times per 100.
spots.fix: No mistake. [[3s]] and [[5s]] were genbutsu against the dealer, but live against kamicha's souzu hand, and they cost a shanten. The one read that could have saved it is the dealer's river: pinzu, souzu and a single manzu, the pattern of a manzu half flush, where honors are the tiles that hit.

spots.title: Fourth, tenpai for third, one live tile
spots.situation: South 4, two honba, turn 18, five tiles left. You are fourth on 12,400. The dealer, kamicha, declared riichi on turn 7 and is third on 19,600, and shimocha has three calls. Your open hand waits on [[3p]] with a pinzu straight and three dora, about 7,700, enough to take third.
spots.did: You pushed the [[7s]] you drew, live against both, and dealt in to the dealer for 12,200. That left you 200 points, and a tsumo in the next hand put you below zero.
spots.luckyj: With 3 or more han on 3 or fewer live tiles, LuckyJ pushes an open tenpai against a riichi 87% of the time.
spots.fix: A close call, not a mistake. Folding with [[1p]], genbutsu against both, kept you alive in fourth for the next hand. Pushing was the only way to take third in this one. From fourth a deal-in cannot cost you a place, which is why this push is defensible and the chun riichi in the first example was not.

spots.title: A 3-han open tenpai pushed against a riichi
spots.situation: East 3, turn 14. You are second on 25,300. Kamicha declared riichi on turn 11, and shimocha and toimen have a call each. Your open tanyao with two dora is tenpai on [[7p]] with 4 live tiles, and you draw [[1p]], live against all three.
spots.did: You pushed it and dealt in to the riichi for 5,200.
spots.luckyj: With 3 or more han and 4 or more live tiles, LuckyJ pushes an open tenpai against a riichi 95% of the time.
spots.fix: No mistake. Every other cut broke the tenpai, and a 3-han hand with a live wait is one to push. Your pushes of these hands deal in 23% of the time, as LuckyJ's do, and this was one of them.

spots.title: A riichi that drew the winning tile
spots.situation: South 2, one honba, turn 12. You are fourth on 14,000, and toimen has one call. You hold a closed chun triplet and draw into tenpai on [[4m]]-[[7m]] with 8 live tiles.
spots.did: You declared riichi with [[6p]]. The next turn you drew [[3m]], toimen's winning tile, and had to cut it: 4,200 and your stick.
spots.luckyj: With nobody in riichi, LuckyJ declares 93% of first closed tenpais with 8 or more live tiles.
spots.fix: No mistake. From fourth the hand needed riichi's value, since dama with the chun alone wins 1,300. Once you are in riichi the drawn tile goes out, and this one hit.
